questions.prompt: Complete: "The head teacher followed the ___ of the health authority and closed the school for a week."
questions.explanation: After "the" the sentence needs a noun, and the noun is "advice", spelt with a c. "Advise", spelt with an s, is the verb — you advise somebody to do something — and neither its -s form nor its -ing form can stand after an article.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My parents ___ in this town since 2019."
questions.explanation: "Since" names the point where the situation started, and a situation that started in the past and is still true today takes the present perfect: have lived. The past simple would cut the link with the present, and neither the present simple nor the present continuous is ever used with since.

questions.prompt: The school nurse said: "I am tired." Which sentence reports her words?

options.text: The nurse said that she is tired.
The nurse said that she was tired.
The nurse said that I was tired.
The nurse said that she has been tired.

questions.explanation: Reporting after a past verb pushes the tense one pace back and moves the pronoun to the reporter's point of view: the present "am" becomes "was" and the speaker's "I" becomes "she". Leaving "is" reports nothing, keeping "I" makes the reporter the tired one, and "has been" changes the meaning to a state going on up to now.

questions.prompt: Which prefix turns "legal" into its opposite?
questions.explanation: The negative prefix takes the form "il-" in front of a word beginning with l: illegal, illiterate, illogical. "Im-" is the form used before m, p and b (impossible, impatient); "un-" and "dis-" attach to plenty of other words (unfair, disobedient) but never produce "unlegal" or "dislegal".

questions.prompt: Your partner writes the letter "S" of the correction code above the word "wich" in your draft. What must you correct?
questions.explanation: In the correction code S stands for a spelling mistake, and "wich" is the word "which" with a letter missing — a mistake inside the word. V would mean you had chosen a word that does not exist or does not fit the meaning, W.O. that the words were in the wrong order, and P that a punctuation mark was wrong.
